sermon.title: 2012 Apostle Two 0219: What Is an Apostle? (Conclusion)
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this concluding message on “What Is an Apostle?” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 1 Corinthians 9:18–27. He says an apostle is a delegated leader under Jesus Christ who makes himself a servant to win people, becomes “all things to all men” without joining their sin, and runs the race with self-control and confidence so that he is not disqualified. He explains the shadow laws and says that salvation requires keeping the qualifications to the end.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: this is the conclusion of a two-part teaching on “What Is an Apostle?”; the earlier part is a separate recording. He mentions a recent celebrity death and two television ministers by name; the names stay in the transcript only, and the garbled ones are marked “[unclear].” He says “once saved always saved” is a lie; this is his view. He makes claims about Jews in Israel and about habits and addiction; these are his words and are not verified by this site. “[Unclear]” marks six spots: two at about 0:55 and one each at about 17:00, 20:45, 21:40 and 22:10.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about leaving the fighting to ministers and disciplining the body?
chunks.short_answer: He says some want ministers “to do our fighting for us,” sending money so someone else will pray, when “you got to fight.” He says Paul disciplines his body and brings it “into subjection,” and that we choose our habits: “you weren’t born that way, you chose that way.” He mentions a recent celebrity death as an example, by name in the transcript only.

And, you know, this is true in America, you know, instead of going to college and learning a degree or, or a technical school and learning a job skill or on-the-job training to learn a good job skill, oh, we just send our money to Benny [unclear] so that God will just rain money from heaven on us. qualifications. He said, “I discipline my body and bring it into subjection,” or bring my body into slavery. I don’t do what my body wants to do, my body does what I wanted to do. “Well, I just, you know, I was just born this way, that I just got to have alcohol, or I got to have drugs,” like they said of, uh, Whitney Houston over the weekend. You weren’t born that way, you chose that way. You got to bring your body into discipline, restrain it, make it a slave of you. When that body doesn’t want to get out of bed and pray, you say, “Body, get out of bed. Arms, lift yourself up. Mouth, move.” And you know what? They obey.

chunks.section_question: What does he say “disqualified” means, and does God empower us to reach the goal?
chunks.short_answer: He says “disqualified” does not mean being benched but “getting kicked off the team.” He says that if Jesus gave us these goals, he empowers us to attain them, as with Abraham’s faith that God “had the power to perform what he promised,” but there are four requirements on our part.

disqualified. Wow. One preacher said it meant he was going to get benched. No, he’s getting kicked off the team, he’s getting kicked out of the gym, he’s getting kicked off the campus, he’s disqualified. He’s not even a benchwarmer. Wow. All of a sudden the things of God are serious, aren’t they? Now, if Jesus gave us these goals, does he empower us to attain to them? Yes. And see, that’s the faith Abraham had that was counted to him for righteousness in Galatians, that he had the faith, he believed that God had the power to perform what he

promised. Now, if God can get us saved, can he keep us sav— and get us to the goal? Does he have the power? Yes. But is there requirements on my part? Yeah. Here’s four of them.

scriptures.text_nkjv: He did not waver at the promise of God through unbelief, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God, and being fully convinced that what He had promised He was also able to perform.

faqs.question: Who does he say the real leader of the church is?
faqs.answer: He says “the real authority, the real boss, is Jesus Christ.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: What is my reward then? That when I preach the gospel, I may present the gospel of Christ without charge, that I may not abuse my authority in the gospel.

faqs.question: Does he say ministers should force people to pay?
faqs.answer: No. He says “you don’t force people to pay anything, they’ve got to do it from the drawing of Christ.”

faqs.question: What is another word he gives for “servant” in 1 Corinthians 9:19?

scriptures.text_nkjv: For though I am free from all men, I have made myself a servant to all, that I might win the more;

faqs.question: What does he mean by shadow laws?
faqs.answer: He says “the sacrifice of the lamb was a shadow, an example of Christ coming to die for us,” and that the incense “was the example of prayer.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Let my prayer be set before You as incense, The lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice.

faqs.question: Does he say the Old Testament civil laws changed?
faqs.answer: No. He says “there are civil laws in the Old Testament which did not change, and then there’s shadow laws.”

faqs.question: Does “all things to all men” mean joining in sin?
faqs.answer: No. He says Paul did not get drunk with drunks, and “common sense tells you that.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: to the weak I became as weak, that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all men, that I might by all means save some.

faqs.question: What does he say a partaker is?
faqs.answer: He says it is not “just a hearer of the goal, not just a talker of the goal” but a “partaker,” and a partaker is “a participant, a reaper of the benefits.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now this I do for the gospel’s sake, that I may be partaker of it with you.

faqs.question: How many receive the prize in a race, according to 1 Corinthians 9:24?
faqs.answer: He says “one,” and “the only guy that was declared the winner was the guy who went across the line first.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Do you not know that those who run in a race all run, but one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may obtain it.

faqs.question: What is the first qualification for the prize?
faqs.answer: He says it is being “temperate,” which he explains means “self-controlled.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And everyone who competes for the prize is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a perishable crown, but we for an imperishable crown.

faqs.question: What does he mean by saying “I’m just a flea on the dog”?
faqs.answer: He is describing a common thing people say about themselves, and says “we all know we’re no good when you stand by Christ,” but “we are in the race to be like him.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.

faqs.question: Does he say we are born with habits we cannot control?
faqs.answer: No. He says “you weren’t born that way, you chose that way,” and that you can “bring your body into discipline.”

faqs.question: Does he say once saved always saved is true?
faqs.answer: No. He says “don’t you believe that big lie,” and that someone who was saved can end up “disqualified.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore I run thus: not with uncertainty. Thus I fight: not as one who beats the air. But I discipline my body and bring it into subjection, lest, when I have preached to others, I myself should become disqualified.
